ai-at-work.title: Coders are refusing to work without AI — and that could come back to bite them
ai-at-work.excerpt: While AI is helping coders produce code faster, it may not be producing better code, researchers warn. And that could cause problems down the road for them.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Developers are increasingly demanding AI tools as a baseline expectation, but the research suggests the code they're producing isn't necessarily better, just faster. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because you're inheriting the technical debt and maintenance headaches when faster code turns out to be sloppier code. Here's the thing: rushing to ship AI-generated anything without quality gates is how you end up explaining to your board why your systems are held together with digital duct tape.

ai-at-work.title: So you’ve heard these AI terms and nodded along; let’s fix that
ai-at-work.excerpt: The rise of AI has brought an avalanche of new terms and slang. Here is a glossary with definitions of some of the most important words and phrases you might encounter.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: TechCrunch published a glossary of AI terminology because the field has exploded with jargon that most people are nodding along to without actually understanding. This matters because digital workplace leaders are being asked to make real decisions about AI tools, vendors, and implementations while drowning in buzzwords like "hallucinations" and "fine-tuning" without solid definitions. Honestly, if you need a glossary to understand what your own tech vendors are selling you, that's less a problem with the vocabulary and more a signal that someone's overselling complexity to cover for underwhelming substance.

ai-at-work.title: Does your CEO have AI psychosis? Aaron Levie thinks most of them do.
ai-at-work.excerpt: The people deciding that AI can replace your job are also the ones least likely to understand what your job truly involves, according to Box founder Aaron Levie, who pointed to this as an example of “
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Aaron Levie is calling out what he sees as CEO delusion around AI capabilities, arguing that executives making AI replacement decisions often don't actually understand the work being done. This matters because digital workplace pros are stuck in the middle between boardroom hype and messy operational reality, watching leaders make sweeping automation bets without understanding what will actually break. The irony is thick: the same executives who claim AI will solve everything are probably the ones least equipped to implement it without torching their organizations in the process.

ai-at-work.title: Nous Research's NousCoder-14B is an open-source coding model landing right in the Claude Code moment
ai-at-work.excerpt: Nous Research, the open-source artificial intelligence startup backed by crypto venture firm Paradigm, released a new competitive programming model on Monday that it says matches or exceeds several la
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Nous Research just dropped NousCoder-14B, an open-source coding model that claims to match bigger proprietary systems while being trained in only four days on a relatively modest GPU setup. This matters because it shows open-source alternatives are finally catching up to Claude and GitHub Copilot, which means your organization actually has real choices instead of being locked into one vendor's vision of how developers should work. The crypto backing is mildly amusing given how many blockchain projects need rescuing from bad code, but hey, at least someone's democratizing AI coding tools.

tools-tech.title: I tried Microsoft's Windows 365 Cloud PC on MacOS, Android, and iOS - here's what it's like
tools-tech.excerpt: Who needs a Cloud PC, anyway? What's the experience like? How much does it really cost? I've got answers to all those questions.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft rolled out Windows 365 Cloud PC across Mac, Android, and iOS devices, and someone actually tested whether it works in the real world. This matters because it shows enterprises can now give remote workers genuine Windows experiences without lugging around hardware, which changes the conversation about BYOD policies and support costs. The real question isn't whether it works technically, it's whether your organization is actually ready to manage cloud-based desktops when half your IT team is still struggling with basic endpoint management on premises.

tools-tech.title: AI hiring monoculture is delivering racial bias at scale
tools-tech.excerpt: A research project examining AI-driven recruitment hires across the US has revealed a systemic racial bias. Researchers from Stanford University found a startling pattern of racial disparities when lo
tools-tech.dwp_take: AI recruiting tools are systematically showing racial bias across thousands of employers, according to Stanford research analyzing 4 million job applications. This matters to digital workplace leaders because you're likely using or evaluating these same tools right now, and deploying biased hiring systems creates legal exposure, talent pipeline problems, and actively harms your workforce diversity efforts. The real kicker is that we've built a monoculture of broken AI tools that most companies are just copy-pasting into their hiring processes without question, which means the bias gets replicated at scale rather than fixed.

tools-tech.title: Certifiably random: Swiss researchers claim perfect random number source
tools-tech.excerpt: Researchers in Switzerland claim to have built a perfect random number generator from two quantum superconducting chips, a 30-meter-long pipe, and some software. The resulting device could be used to
tools-tech.dwp_take: Swiss researchers built a quantum random number generator using superconducting chips and claim it's genuinely perfect, unlike previous attempts that always had some bias. This matters because cryptographic security depends on actual randomness, and if your encryption keys come from a fake random source, your whole security posture is built on sand. That said, I'll believe it when every major tech company and security firm independently verifies it, because "we fixed randomness" is about as common in research papers as "we cured cancer."

tools-tech.title: Why AI can’t match human creative work
tools-tech.excerpt: It’s hard for people to tell the difference between AI-generated advertising and writing. So why do they respond better to the human-made stuff? AI vs. Mad Men Ipsos, along with faculty members from S
tools-tech.dwp_take: A new Ipsos study shows people can't easily spot the difference between AI-generated and human-created ads, yet they still prefer and respond better to the human-made versions. This matters to digital workplace pros because it cuts through the AI hype around "replacing creative workers" and shows that audiences actually value the human element even when they can't articulate why. The real takeaway: your marketing team isn't getting replaced by ChatGPT tomorrow, but they do need to understand how to work alongside these tools instead of against them.

digital-culture.title: Should you take a soft off day?
digital-culture.excerpt: From doing laundry to flying to Europe, all while on the company clock. The soft off day is a remote work habit that’s everywhere right now. Is it time theft or just surviving burnout culture? Here’s
digital-culture.dwp_take: Remote workers are quietly taking partial days off while staying logged in, doing personal errands or even traveling without formally clocking out. This matters because it's a symptom of how broken our work culture has become, creating legal exposure for companies and ethical gray zones for employees who are frankly exhausted. My take: stop pretending this is clever and instead actually fix the real problem, which is that people are so burned out they need to steal time just to survive their jobs.

digital-culture.title: Workforce data, smarter AI integration among greatest workplace priorities in the new year
digital-culture.excerpt: The importance of workforce data is just one of the prognostications people managers are making looking to the year ahead.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies are planning to lean harder on workforce data and AI tools to make decisions about their employees in 2025. This matters because digital workplace leaders are now the gatekeepers of the infrastructure that feeds these systems, which means they own both the opportunity and the risk when data goes wrong. Here's the thing though: most organizations still can't get basic employee directory data clean, so "smarter AI integration" is probably going to be garbage in, garbage out until someone actually fixes the fundamentals first.

digital-culture.title: ‘Bah, humbug!’ Could employee apathy mean curtains for the traditional holiday party?
digital-culture.excerpt: People say they prefer cash or time off, though some argue office gatherings are still beneficial
digital-culture.dwp_take: Employees increasingly skip traditional holiday parties in favor of cash bonuses or extra time off, signaling a real shift in what workers actually value. This matters because it forces digital workplace leaders to rethink how they build culture and connection, especially when remote and hybrid work already fragment team cohesion. Honestly, if your culture strategy depends on forcing people to stand around a conference room eating stale cookies while making small talk, you had bigger problems than apathy anyway.

digital-culture.title: As employer burnout costs soar, EY gets at the heart of worker well-being with Vitality Index
digital-culture.excerpt: The tool is designed to help employers measure and boost workforce well-being.
digital-culture.dwp_take: EY launched the Vitality Index, a measurement tool aimed at helping employers track and improve workforce well-being as burnout costs continue climbing. This matters because digital workplace leaders are increasingly expected to own employee experience metrics beyond just tech adoption, and burnout directly impacts productivity, retention, and your ability to attract talent. The real question is whether another well-being index actually changes behavior or just gives executives another dashboard to ignore while they quietly pile on more work.

industry-news.title: Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin Faces Setback After New Glenn Rocket Explodes
industry-news.excerpt: Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket exploded during a Florida ground test, leaving crews to assess launch-site damage, debris risks, and the cause of the fireball. The post Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin Faces Se
industry-news.dwp_take: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket caught fire during a ground test in Florida, destroying the vehicle and forcing investigators to assess damage and debris. This matters to digital workplace pros because space companies rely on robust testing protocols and incident documentation systems that your organization probably uses too, just with lower stakes. If Bezos can't keep a rocket from exploding on the ground, at least we know IT's infrastructure disasters are more forgivable by comparison.

industry-news.title: AI Data Centers Now Account for 17% of Australia’s Private Investment
industry-news.excerpt: Australia’s AI data center boom drove private investment sharply higher, even as weaker household spending exposed a widening economic split. The post AI Data Centers Now Account for 17% of Australia’
industry-news.dwp_take: Australia is plowing massive private capital into AI data centers at a scale that would make most sectors jealous, with these facilities now representing 17% of all private investment. For digital workplace leaders, this signals that AI infrastructure spending is real money with real consequences for everything from cloud services to compliance obligations in your region. The funny part is watching organizations scramble to build AI strategies when the actual infrastructure race is already well underway, which means you're either in it or you're explaining to your board why you're not.

industry-news.title: Dexcom Warns Stolen G7 Glucose Sensors May Pose Infection, Reading Risks
industry-news.excerpt: Dexcom says stolen G7 sensors from two scrapped lots were sold through unauthorized channels, creating infection and reading-failure risks. The post Dexcom Warns Stolen G7 Glucose Sensors May Pose Inf
industry-news.dwp_take: Dexcom had two batches of G7 glucose sensors stolen from scrap lots and sold on the black market, potentially exposing users to infections and faulty readings. For digital workplace professionals managing health tech deployments or employee wellness programs, this is a reminder that device security extends well beyond software to physical supply chains and asset management. The lesson here is brutal: you can't just toss medical devices in a dumpster and hope for the best, which apparently needed saying.

industry-news.title: iOS 27 Rumor: Siri Could Become Apple’s Answer to ChatGPT
industry-news.excerpt: iOS 27 could bring a rebuilt Siri, Dynamic Island AI search, chatbot-style tools, and deeper AI features across iPhone apps. The post iOS 27 Rumor: Siri Could Become Apple’s Answer to ChatGPT appeared
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple is apparently rebuilding Siri with AI capabilities similar to ChatGPT for iOS 27, along with adding chatbot-style tools and deeper AI integration across iPhone apps. This matters because your workforce already relies on iPhones and iPads, and a smarter Siri could change how employees search, get information, and interact with business apps on mobile devices. The real question is whether Apple will actually make Siri useful this time around, or if we'll just get another feature that everyone ignores in favor of asking ChatGPT directly.
